hypothesis: If only the deer has cranial appendages that are solid throughout and branched, and only the deer sheds them, annually, unless castrated, then a comparative review of extant ruminant headgear will assign solid-and-branched and annual shedding to cervid antlers alone, and a castration account will say that castrated deer do not keep the normal annual casting of hardened antlers.
pass_criterion: All three clauses pass. (1) Solid and branched: among the four extant types antler, bovid horn, pronghorn and ossicone, only the antler is coded solid-throughout and branched. (2) Shedding: only the antler is coded as shed or annually replaced, counting an annually shed keratin sheath as shedding. (3) Castration: the castration text says castrated male deer fail to complete the normal annual cycle of hardening and casting, for example by retaining velvet or by not regrowing a normal hardened antler the next year, and it does not say that castrates cast and regrow hardened antlers on the ordinary annual schedule.
fail_criterion: Any one of the three clauses fails: a non-antler type is solid-throughout and branched, a non-antler type is shed or annually replaced, or castrates are described as keeping the normal annual cast of hardened antlers. If clause 1 or 2 cannot be coded from the headgear review, the verdict is inconclusive with reason data-unavailable. If clauses 1 and 2 pass and the castration text cannot be found, the verdict is inconclusive with reason data-unavailable. A failed clause is a refutation even if another clause is uncoded.
interpretation: 'Stag' and 'deer' are read as cervids, not one species, because the claim contrasts the stag with all other animals and the scope says deer versus other horned animals. 'Solid throughout' means the appendage itself is bone, not a keratin sheath over a bony core. 'Branched' means the appendage or its sheath has branches. 'Sheds its horns' includes annual loss of a keratin sheath, because that sheath is the horn an observer sees. Castration is the removal of the testes. Giraffe ossicones and bovid horns are in scope as other horned animals.

test_contract.expected_observation: Antlers alone are both solid bone and branched, antlers alone are shed or replaced annually, and castration stops the normal annual casting of hardened antlers.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: Another extant headgear type is solid and branched, or is shed or annually replaced, or castrated deer continue the ordinary annual casting of hardened antlers.
test_contract.admissible_datasets: Open full texts of comparative reviews that describe structure and shedding for the extant ruminant headgear types, plus an open account of castration experiments or clinical castrates in deer. Specimen photographs without a coded comparison are not sufficient.
test_contract.inference_method: Code each of the four types from the headgear review with pre-registered string rules, and code the castration clause from sentences that contain 'castrat'. A conjunction fails if any clause fails. No vote across papers beyond the two named sources.
